newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panamanian marchers blast government, burn effigy.
newsitem.headline: Panamanian marchers blast government, burn effigy.

text.p: Hundreds of Panamanian workers showed their disgust with the government's economic measures on Wednesday by blocking traffic and burning an effigy of Planning and Economic Policy Minister Guillermo Chapman, officials said.

Nearly 1,000 government employees, including teachers and nurses, protested the economic initiatives of the administration of President Ernesto Perez Balladares, particularly plans to cap a deficit in a special retirement fund they are entitled to, local RPC television reported in a live broadcast on Wednesday.

In a park near the presidential palace, the protesters burned an effigy of Chapman, the man charged with carrying out the nation's economic programmes and averting a deficit in the special retirement fund, RPC reported.
"We presented a document to the government telling them not to get rid of this fund," union leader Domingo Sanchez told RPC.
Perez Balladares told reporters earlier on Wednesday that he has no plans to end the special retirement fund, but said the fund is running a deficit of $60 million.
"I am willing to sit down and discuss ways to save the fund," the president said.
